notices.text: Cube positions are the laboratory lattice moved by the event's D-frame motion (the midpoint of the two back-projected entry points to the origin, A→B along +x′), computed from the lattice as the ensemble D-frame is; the per-shower coordinate columns are not read.

Per-axis half-widths: each axis's own energy-weighted 0.1st–99.9th percentile range of the drawn showers' cells in this frame, plus one cell footprint across the beam and one layer pitch along depth, so the cells at either end are drawn whole, never below 150 mm and snapped outward to 20 mm (x′ 2,120 mm, y′ 1,000 mm, z′ 600 mm here). The box keeps one scale on all three axes (1:1:1), so each side is as long as its axis's span; the paired projections take the same rule; symmetric about the origin across the beam; cells snap it to whole cells, voxels to whole bins. The cells beyond it are counted with the cap, below.

Logarithmic ramp of the volumetric energy density E/V in GeV per mm³, from the 1st percentile of the drawn 20 mm voxels' positive densities (1.91e−11) to the brightest drawn voxel (5.37e−07). The floor is the voxels' own, not the cells': a voxel holds only the part of a moved footprint that overlaps it, so voxel densities run below cell densities, and a floor from the cells would draw a sparse shower wholly at the lowest colour; 60 voxels below the floor are drawn at the lowest colour and flagged.

The notebook's C5 display colours each hit's raw energy on a linear ramp with no floor; this view colours volumetric density on a logarithmic ramp with the 1st-percentile floor of its A1/C2 figure, because cell energies span many decades.

The 6,000 most energetic of 8,743 voxels inside the window are drawn (cap 6,000, ranked by energy); the 2,743 beyond the cap hold 6.064e−05 GeV, 0.0145% of the drawn showers' energy, counted and not drawn. 3 of the event's 921 cells lie outside the window and are counted, not drawn. 0.0004233 GeV (0.101%) falls outside the window and is counted, not drawn.

window.rule: Per-axis half-widths: each axis's own energy-weighted 0.1st–99.9th percentile range of the drawn showers' cells in this frame, plus one cell footprint across the beam and one layer pitch along depth, so the cells at either end are drawn whole, never below 150 mm and snapped outward to 20 mm (x′ 2,120 mm, y′ 1,000 mm, z′ 600 mm here). The box keeps one scale on all three axes (1:1:1), so each side is as long as its axis's span; the paired projections take the same rule; symmetric about the origin across the beam; cells snap it to whole cells, voxels to whole bins. The cells beyond it are counted with the cap, below.

depth.note: the detector's own sampling layers, z′ = z − z_front; the index is the layer ordinal, placed through axes.z.coords

geometry.note: In this frame each cell is turned about the detector axis by the event's D-frame rotation R_z(ψ), and an echarts-gl bar3D cube cannot tilt. Each cell's 48.27 × 48.60 × 20.5 mm footprint is therefore split into 12 × 12 equal sub-deposits that move with it, binned onto axis-aligned 20 × 20 × 20.5 mm voxels: energy is conserved, and k is chosen so the voxels converge on the footprints' area overlap (k = 4, enough for a projected panel, leaves empty voxels in 3-D). A voxel's centre is grid.x0 + (index + 0.5) × pitch along x and y, and axes.z.coords[index] along depth.

shower_codes: energy from rows of more than one origin

scale.floor_rule: Logarithmic ramp of the volumetric energy density E/V in GeV per mm³, from the 1st percentile of the drawn 20 mm voxels' positive densities (1.91e−11) to the brightest drawn voxel (5.37e−07).
